citation: Brehm A, Liu Y, Sheikh A, Marrero B, Omoyinmi E, Zhou Q, et al. Additive loss-of-function proteasome subunit mutations in CANDLE/PRAAS patients promote type I IFN production. The Journal of Clinical Investigation. 2015. doi:10.1172/JCI81260.
description: This study identified human loss-of-function mutations in proteasome genes including PSMB4 and showed that the variants impair proteasome assembly and activity. siRNA depletion of proteasome subunits in control fibroblasts recapitulated the proteasome defect, and patient cells plus experimentally impaired control cells induced a type-I-interferon transcriptional program.

citation: Radhakrishnan SK, Lee CS, Young P, Beskow A, Chan JY, Deshaies RJ. Transcription factor Nrf1 mediates the proteasome recovery pathway after proteasome inhibition in mammalian cells. Molecular Cell. 2010. doi:10.1016/j.molcel.2010.02.029.
description: The paper showed that mammalian cells transcriptionally increase proteasome subunit genes after proteasome inhibition and that Nrf1, rather than Nrf2, is required for this recovery response. It supplies the directionally interpretable link from impaired proteasome activity to increased Psmc/Psmd/Psme proteasome-pathway transcripts.

citation: Teske BF, Fusakio ME, Zhou D, Shan J, McClintick JN, Kilberg MS, Wek RC. CHOP induces activating transcription factor 5 to trigger apoptosis in response to perturbations in protein homeostasis. Molecular Biology of the Cell. 2013. doi:10.1091/mbc.E13-01-0067.
description: This study linked proteasome inhibition to the integrated stress response, CHOP/DDIT3 induction, ATF5 activation, and apoptosis-related transcription. It supports the expected increase of Ddit3 and pro-apoptotic ISR genes after proteasome impairment.
